title: Go: Sorting
description: Sort slices in Go using built-in and custom sorting with the sort package.

steps.title: sort.Ints and sort.Strings
steps.description: Create an unsorted slice of `[]int{5, 2, 8, 1, 9}` and `[]string{"dog", "cat", "bird"}`. Use `sort.Ints` and `sort.Strings` to sort them and print both sorted slices.

verification.failureMessage: Use sort.Ints and sort.Strings on your slices.

steps.title: sort.Slice custom
steps.description: Given a slice of `Person` structs (Name, Age), use `sort.Slice` to sort by Age ascending. Print each person after sorting. People: [{Alice 30}, {Bob 25}, {Charlie 35}].
hints: `sort.Slice(people, func(i, j int) bool { return people[i].Age < people[j].Age })`
The less function returns true if element i should come before j

verification.successMessage: Custom sort by age! Bob (25) < Alice (30) < Charlie (35)
verification.failureMessage: The less function should compare people[i].Age and people[j].Age.

steps.title: sort.SliceStable
steps.description: Sort a slice of `Task` structs (Name string, priority int) first by priority ascending. Use `sort.SliceStable` so equal-priority items keep original order. Tasks: "low"(1), "medium"(2), "high"(1).
hints: `sort.SliceStable` preserves original order of equal elements
Use the same less function signature as sort.Slice
Compare behavior with sort.Slice when priorities are equal

verification.successMessage: Stable sort preserved order of equal-priority items!
verification.failureMessage: Use sort.SliceStable with the priority comparison.

steps.title: Sort with custom interface
steps.description: Define a `type ByLength []string` and implement `sort.Interface` (Len, Less, Swap) to sort strings by length (shortest first). Sort `["apple", "banana", "kiwi", "grape"]` and print.

verification.failureMessage: Implement all three methods of sort.Interface.

steps.title: sort.Reverse
steps.description: Sort a slice `[]int{3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9}` in descending order using `sort.Sort(sort.Reverse(sort.IntSlice(nums)))`. Print the reversed slice.
hints: `sort.Reverse` wraps any sort.Interface and reverses the Less function
`sort.IntSlice` is a type that satisfies sort.Interface
